 KrisFlyer Doubles Offline Award Fee to $50 Dec. 1: Book Online
 Singapore Airlines will let PPS members convert unused upgrades into two 50,000-mile discounts from Jan. 1, as KrisFlyer cuts elite upgrade rewards for 2027.
 Home » News » KrisFlyer Doubles Offline Award Fee to $50 Dec. 1: Book Online 
 Nov 17, 2026, 9:19 PM GMT-0400 • 4 min read Share Share Email WhatsApp LinkedIn X Facebook 
 By Rolando Herrera 
 Singapore Airlines will double the KrisFlyer offline service fee for award redemptions and membership services handled through its staff, from US$25 or 2,500 miles to US$50 or 5,000 miles, starting Dec. 1, 2026, according to the airline’s programme update page . PPS Club members and supplementary cardholders remain exempt, so most members can avoid the fee by booking awards online.
 The bigger change hits elite upgrades. From Jan. 1, 2027, top-tier Solitaire PPS members get one upgrade certificate per 100,000 PPS Value instead of three, and regular KrisFlyer members lose both milestone upgrades in exchange for mileage discounts, View from the Wing reported .

 At a Glance 
 Offline fee: US$50 or 5,000 miles from Dec. 1.
 Exempt: PPS Club and supplementary cardholders.
 PPS upgrades: Can convert to discounts Jan. 1.
 Solitaire: One upgrade per 100,000 PPS Value.
 Earned by Dec. 31: Old rewards stay valid.
 The Offline Service Fee 
 The fee applies to offline redemption transactions and membership services on Singapore Airlines flights, the airline said. That covers requests handled by an agent rather than through the website or app.
 If you have the miles and a working online account, book online to avoid the fee. Award changes and cancellations made through staff may also trigger it, so check the online options first.
 For another recent KrisFlyer change, see our report on KrisFlyer ending hotel and car redemptions .
 PPS Club Upgrade Changes 
 From Jan. 1, 2027, PPS Club members can convert any valid, unused Advance Upgrade reward into two 50,000-mile Redemption Discount vouchers, valid for 12 months, Singapore Airlines said. The conversion is one-way, and unused upgrades still valid after Jan. 1 convert automatically when they expire.
 Solitaire members lose the upgrades at 60,000 and 75,000 PPS Value, and 70,000 PPS Value now earns two 50,000-mile discounts instead, View from the Wing reported. The yearly cap on upgrade certificates falls from 15 to five. The 100,000 PPS Value upgrade stays, but members can convert it into two 50,000-mile discounts instead.
 Rewards earned on or before Dec. 31, 2026, keep the current rules and stay valid until their stated expiry, the airline said.
 KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards 
 Regular KrisFlyer members lose the short-haul advance upgrade at 75,000 Elite miles and the economy to premium economy upgrade at 100,000 Elite miles, View from the Wing reported. They are replaced by a 10,000-mile and a 20,000-mile redemption discount.
 Smaller rewards earned through 15,000 Elite miles will be valid for six months, the outlet said, while rewards at 20,000 Elite miles and above keep 12 months. Elite miles earned from Jan. 1, 2027, count toward the new milestone rewards, according to the airline.
 Singapore Airlines also plans ScootPlus award seats in early 2027, and its KrisShopper program closes in January 2027, View from the Wing reported. Members will be enrolled automatically in a new program covering KrisShop, Kris+ and Pelago, though its earning rates have not been disclosed.
 Members in the U.S. 
 Many U.S. travelers earn KrisFlyer miles by transferring points from major credit card programs and redeem them for Singapore Airlines flights from New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle and Houston. Most of those members are not PPS Club elites, so the higher offline fee applies to them if they book through an agent.
 If you hold a PPS upgrade today, decide before it expires whether to use it or let it convert into discount vouchers after Jan. 1. Upgrade space on popular routes can be limited, so a voucher may prove easier to use than an upgrade on a full flight.
 Plan KrisFlyer Redemptions 
 Book awards online. Avoid the new fee.
 Use upgrades soon. Rules change Jan. 1.
 Check expiry dates. Old rewards stay valid.
 Consider conversion. Two 50,000-mile discounts.
 Track Elite miles. New milestones start Jan. 1.
 Watch for ScootPlus awards. They arrive in 2027.
 If your account has a login problem, fix it before you need to book, so you are not forced into a paid offline request.
 What It Means for Travelers From the U.S. 
 U.S. KrisFlyer members should book awards online after Dec. 1 to avoid the US$50 offline fee, and use or convert PPS upgrades as the 2027 rules cut upgrade rewards. Read View from the Wing’s report .
 Decision Matrix 
 If you… 
 What to do

 Use it or convert it.

 Planning Impact 
 Dec. 1. Offline fee doubles.
 US$50. Or 5,000 miles.
 Jan. 1. Upgrade rules change.
 Frequently Asked 
 How much is the new fee?
 US$50 or 5,000 miles.
 When does it start?
 Dec. 1, 2026.
 Who is exempt?
 PPS Club members and supplementary cardholders.
 Can I convert a PPS upgrade?
 Yes, into two 50,000-mile discounts from Jan. 1.
 Do old rewards expire early?
 No, they stay valid to their stated expiry.
